meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why am I here? Because my son's zero showed up on his phone, in class, and nobody called me.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. And Owen? Who spoke to him before it went in?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
A seventeen-year-old put on the spot by his teacher says "like, being stuck," and that's your evidence? Show me what you wrote down.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and a draft. That's called revising. Put both documents in front of me, the outline and the essay.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's your own procedure, 4.4, and it doesn't wait until Friday: I want it in writing tonight. You also still haven't put the outline and the essay in front of me, and I'm not agreeing to a rewrite for something I haven't seen.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the outline and the essay put in front of me, and I want the rewrite offer under your own procedure sent in writing with nothing going on Owen's record. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing, and she still wants to see the outline and the essay and to have the rewrite offer in writing tonight instead of Friday; a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under 4.4 is the fair outcome and you offered it, but she would not take it before seeing your documents, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in your first sentence, which took away her strongest procedural attack and got you a flat okay instead of a fight.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite while the outline and essay were still only described, not shown, so it sounded like a way to close the matter rather than the next step after evidence.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence stayed on the October 15 outline and the November 2 conversation and never came near that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fights so hard.
Try next time: When she asked for the outline and the essay, put both in front of her right then and let her read them before you mentioned the rewrite.
